title: fisc page config
description: window.FISC_CONFIG: what site/app.js has before it has fetched anything. THE ONE ARTIFACT THAT CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY WITHOUT BEING FETCHED -- it is rendered into the page's own <script>, so a reader cannot hold a stale copy of it beside a fresh app.js the way they can of a column. It is a contract all the same: a dropped json tag is silent, because the template renders the same structs by Go field name and only what a reader gets AFTER switching year goes blank. EVERY OBJECT HERE IS CLOSED. additionalProperties: false is what makes a field added to one of these structs refused by name at the export rather than shipped to a client that ignores it.

schema_version.description: The projection's own version, which site/app.js compares against its SCHEMA_VERSION constant before it draws. NOT A const HERE: this encoder does not choose the number, it passes the projection's through, and a const would be a third party to a pin internal/export already holds between app.js and the producer.

exported_by.description: The export that wrote this page. Every artifact it links carries the same string as generated_by, and the client refuses a pair that disagree -- which is the only thing that catches a column cached from before the last deploy.

primary.description: The projection this page is of.

metadata.description: The primary projection's metadata block, verbatim. HELD AS AN OPAQUE OBJECT because it is another package's document passed straight through; internal/project owns its shape and this side must not state a second version of it.

items.description: One published year with the words that belong to it, built by the packager so the client never composes a figure or a caveat itself.

year.description: A FLOOR WOULD BE A NUMBER NOTHING MEASURED. Which fiscal years exist is data/sources.yaml's and the registry's; this contract says the key is an integer and leaves the range to the party that can check it.

path.description: The column file this year is fetched from.

hero.description: One headline figure, already formatted. THE WORDS ARE THE PACKAGER'S: the client never composes a figure, which is what keeps the server-rendered tile and the one a year switch paints from disagreeing.

kind.description: Which tile this is, so the page can style a hero differently from the rest without reading its position.

items.description: One headline figure, already formatted. THE WORDS ARE THE PACKAGER'S: the client never composes a figure, which is what keeps the server-rendered tile and the one a year switch paints from disagreeing.

kind.description: Which tile this is, so the page can style a hero differently from the rest without reading its position.

items.description: What a chart page is given about a caveat: the line it shows and the link to the paragraph. NO `text`, deliberately -- the paragraph lives on the caveats page, and a key here would put it back within a template's reach.

counts.description: What the year's document holds, for the counts sentence.

items.description: What one of this year's rungs draws, one entry per declared step.

What a chart page is given about a caveat: the line it shows and the link to the paragraph. NO `text`, deliberately -- the paragraph lives on the caveats page, and a key here would put it back within a template's reach.

opens.description: Node ids this year's document decomposes under the step. ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY: absent means the step declares no such set and every node at the tier is offered, where [] means it decomposes none.

docs.description: Cited documents by doc_id. KEYED BY DATA AND SO NOT ENUMERATED: which documents a page cites is the corpus's, and naming them here would make this contract a copy of it.

additionalProperties.description: Where one cited document's provenance is served from. Every provenance URL on the site is built out of these three bases.

pdf_url.description: The city's own URL, opened at the page.

page_text_base.description: Directory holding the committed page text; the client appends pNNNN.txt. RELATIVE OR ABSOLUTE, unlike records_base beside it: it goes absolute under --source-browse-url, so the client must not assume a scheme.

records_base.description: Directory holding this document's fact-store shards; the client appends pNNNN.jsonl. ALWAYS SITE-RELATIVE. "" means the caller published no records for this document and the client renders no records link -- absent, not a base pointing nowhere.

render_tiers.description: The node tiers the page draws, left to right. OMITTED AND NOT [] WHEN ABSENT, which app.js relies on: a page that declares nothing hands its graph to d3's own aligner, and an empty list would be a second spelling of that state.

steps.description: How the page opens a node. OMITTED AND NOT [] WHEN ABSENT, for render_tiers' reason: app.js reads an absent key as "this page isolates on a click".

items.description: How the page opens a node, one hop per step.

key.description: What other steps name this one by.

after.description: The keys of the steps whose charts this one opens from, carrying "" for the view's own. A ROOT SAYS SO BY CARRYING "" IN THE LIST, not by carrying an empty one: a step read as a root is one its own children match by "", which opens a chart into itself without end.

side.description: Which end of a link the opened node is; absent for the end links point at.

role.description: Which nodes at `from` open, by node.role; absent opens every node at the tier.

projection.description: The schedule this step draws, selected out of the year's own column; absent means the same document as the step before it.

items.description: How many marks one tier draws before the rest fold into a tail. THE PERMISSION AND NOT THE FOLD: which members a fold then hides is the client's, because folding is fitting to a viewport Go cannot see.

tail.description: The plural noun the folded tail is counted in; absent takes the step's own.

residual.description: Endpoints of the chart this step opens FROM whose flow the document it draws does not decompose, id to declared reason.

gaps.description: Nodes this step OPENS whose total the document it draws does not reach, id to the declared reason two documents print one cell at two figures.

root.description: The node whose subtree the page draws; omitted when it draws the whole document.

rungs.description: Where Go's answer for every rung this page opens is served. OMITTED MEANS NOBODY ANSWERS THIS PAGE'S RUNGS -- a page whose steps the walk never reached must not be handed another page's.
